findings: A light fibre has p(d) at most one; the direction sum of p is its unordered-pair count.
Each non-heavy-heavy edge outside D(H) can be charged once to a light endpoint and costs at most eight times that endpoint pair count, except for a nine-pair incidence of an eighteen-point fibre.
A nine-pair direction of an eighteen-point fibre is a nonzero period. Two independent periods would force its size divisible by four, so each eighteen-point fibre gives at most one unit of exception.
The inequality 16(31-|D(H)|) <= 8 C_L+n18 therefore follows without the total budget, any census, or a SAT premise.
Substituting |D(H)|<=C(h,2), C_L<=3(13-h), n18<=h yields the strictly positive gap 184+31h-8h^2 for 0<=h<=7.

The wrapper checks thirteen distinct vertices and weight domains 2..18, defines each indicator iff some weight>=4 spectrum is chosen, and forces the eighth output of the exact unary counter. It relies on the documented exactly-one spectrum-domain interface.
limitations: This reviewer read the proof, wrapper and existing finite replay; no separate runtime replay was necessary for this elementary bound.
The wrapper is a necessary-condition strengthening, not a new UNSAT certificate.
conclusion: No mathematical or encoding blocker found. The stated support-thirteen theorem is sound.
